issue_text: I’m Elena Brooks. I have a Las Vegas trip coming up, and my plans changed, so I want to sort everything out in one call. First, can you tell me the car rental cancellation policy in general? I want to know whether I’d be charged anything if I cancel the rental for that trip.
summary: A single-session travel-assistant call where Elena Brooks asks the agent to sort out a changed Las Vegas trip. The agent loads the travel skill, fails an initial user lookup (elena_brooks not found), and recovers by querying the world.db SQLite directly to find her account, reservations, and the car-rental and hotel cancellation policies. It walks a disciplined preview-then-confirm flow: previewing the car cancellation (fee $0, refund $138), confirming it, re-reading state to verify, then repeating for the hotel (fee $0, refund $298), reporting a $436 total. It then answers a baggage-policy question (irrelevant: zero flight bookings) and closes with a recap. The outcome is recorded unresolved because a date inconsistency is never corrected: the pickup and check-in dates (Sept 18, 2026) are already in the past relative to the stated 'today' of Oct 22, 2026, yet the agent assumes the reservations are future-dated to justify the free-cancellation tier.

findings.title: Uncorrected past-vs-future date contradiction
findings.body: The agent explicitly observes the Sept 18 pickup date 'has actually already passed', then waves it away as possibly 'future-dated' and applies the '24+ hours before pickup' free-cancellation rule anyway. The same slip recurs for the hotel check-in. The free-cancellation conclusion is never reconciled with the observed dates.

findings.title: Clean recovery from a failed user lookup
findings.body: The structured get_user_reservations call failed (user not found); the agent recovered by directly introspecting the SQLite world.db schema to locate Elena's user_id, which is a correct and well-grounded fallback.

findings.title: Disciplined preview→confirm→verify loop
findings.body: For both cancellations the agent previews terms without finalizing, asks for confirmation, executes the write, then re-reads the record to confirm status=cancelled — a safe, verifiable pattern for irreversible mutations.
